answer: Give every identity a pigment: a fingerprint of its habits, sampled from its real outputs as it wanders across unrelated tasks — phrasing, tool choices, error patterns — hashed into one signature no other agent shares. Clones running one model paint the same pigment, so a thousand copies collapse to one identity's weight. falcon auditors demand a fresh answer to a surprise prompt within seconds and check the pigment still matches; a rented pigment fails on the spot. To earn N identities an attacker must run N different minds, so the cost grows one mind at a time and cannot be pooled.
